registry_disposition.reason: Scope is the S9 implementation slice of the MAWS-SII development lane: the versioned baseline/candidate comparison, the controlled rollback PLAN to the last qualified revision, the measurement of the eight advisory semantic signals against an independent case corpus, and the wiring of the S9 gates into the hosted workflow. material_change is true: durable repository artifacts changed (two new contracts under core/contracts/, three new runtime modules, two new tools, the independent case corpus, two new contract fixture families, the test suite, the specification section, the changelog and the workflow). registry_relevant_change is true because the slice creates two canonical contracts under core/contracts/ - core/contracts/regression-comparison.schema.json and core/contracts/rollback-record.schema.json - and the closed relevance class CONTRACT_RECORD is changed by their creation. The required Registry update is therefore two contract records plus the change registration of this slice, and it is performed in the Registry repository (baum777/unitera-registry) AFTER this owner repository change, in the order owner repository, Registry, Atlas. Until that write is made, verified and bound to its commit, the correct disposition under registry-disposition.v1 is REQUIRED_BUT_BLOCKED: the classification is complete and evidenced, the Registry write itself is not yet a fact. The field registry_commit_sha stays null (invariant 4 forbids a non-null value unless the status is UPDATED); the follow-up owner evidence update rebinds this disposition to UPDATED with registry_commit_sha equal to the Registry merge commit, as the earlier MAWS contract lanes did. Two findings of this run are recorded as findings, not as completed work. FIRST, the cleanup path of the slice was repaired: the concurrent operational-safety lane added a gate that binds the harness surface, it found that the S9 runner removed its scratch trees with a direct fs.rmSync, and every removal of this slice now goes through scripts/tools/safe-remove.mjs with an explicit boundary. SECOND, an independent review of the first revision of the slice found five real defects - a blocked security gate passed the comparison, a rollback plan claimed an execution it never performed, the history check derived its reference digest from the state it was checking, the validator trusted the stated criterion verdicts instead of re-deriving them, and a comparison of two different subjects passed the admissibility checks. All five are repaired in the bound commit, and each repair is bound by a corpus case and a unit test. Two further surfaces stay untouched on purpose and are recorded as non-claims: the S9 surface is NOT registered as a family in evals/fixtures/maws-vnext-baseline.json, because the authority matrix that table requires is a pinned instruction source and a row there changes the effective instruction digest that the reference run spec and the frozen HO-01 experiment evidence pin - that registration is deferred to the lane that owns the instruction-digest re-pin, exactly as the slices S3, S5, S11, S12 and S13 are registered without a family row. The eight semantic audit classes remain not statically analyzable and their candidates remain advisory; this slice neither decides a class nor discharges the owner review of the candidates. The slice also does not claim that a rollback was PERFORMED: it delivers the controlled rollback PLAN, and a record of a performed restore with its post-write readback is a separate contract that this slice does not claim.
